description: Machine-readable registry of all Pathway design system components. AI agents building products read this to discover available components, their props, and their file locations.

sidenav.description: Persistent vertical navigation panel. Two levels of depth, expanded/collapsed states, responsive (push/overlay/hidden). Optional NavSectionLabel headings + optional SideNavListSection for contextual link lists.

scrollbar.description: System-wide overlay scrollbar. error.description: Error / negative styling, fill and border switch to negative token family

highlight.description: Tinted background on the state-layer at rest: for selectable rows

secondary.description: Secondary indeterminate variant (muted colour), use with indeterminate only

disabled.description: Non-interactive; still accessible to screen readers

size.description: Visual size of the control. Touch target is always 44×44px.

onChange.description: Called on user interaction with the new checked value

className.description: Additional CSS class on the root element

describedBy.description: aria-describedby pointing to an error message element (error state)

checkbox.moduleNote: FIXED 2026-10-02: the checked glyph was bound to foreground-action-primary-ON-SUBTLE-rest while the box is filled with fill-action-primary-strong-*, so the tick was #345499 on #3a5aaa, a 1.12:1 contrast, and the whole square read as a solid blue block with no visible tick. Same bug on the error variant: #722121 on #b03a3a at 1.80:1. Both now use the ON-STRONG foreground, which is #ffffff in BOTH modes: 6.52:1 and 5.98:1 in Light, 5.62:1 and 5.98:1 in Midnight. Figma binds Foreground/Static/Neutral/MONO for the tick, which is correct in Light but wrong in Midnight, because mono is an INVERSION ANCHOR rather than a rung and flips to #181b2b, putting a near-black tick on a blue box at 3.04:1. on-strong is the right token for a foreground on a strong fill. See figmaDefect.
checkbox.figmaDefect: The checked glyph binds Foreground/Static/Neutral/Mono. That is correct in Light (#ffffff) and wrong in Midnight: mono is an inversion anchor, not a rung, so it resolves to #181b2b and puts a near-black tick on a blue box (3.04:1). It should be Foreground/Action/Primary/On Strong, which is #ffffff in both modes. The same applies to the error variants, which should use Foreground/Action/Status/Negative/On Strong. The repo already uses the on-strong tokens.

org-switcher.description: Organisation context switcher trigger in the brand-blue top nav. Renders the active org name (truncated with ellipsis at 180px desktop / 50px mobile). For Catholic organisations only, a second container after the org name shows the city or diocese. The trigger opens a drop panel listing accessible orgs.

button.description: Primary action trigger. Three styles (Fill / Outlined / Naked), four semantic types (Primary / Secondary / Tertiary / Negative), four sizes (L / M / S / XS). Supports leading icon, trailing icon, icon-only, and loading states. 48×48px touch target always.

buttonStyle.description: Visual style. Fill = solid surface (highest weight). Outlined = bordered transparent. Naked = no border or fill (lowest weight).

size.description: L = 18px label, M = 16px label, S = 14px label, XS = 12px label (8/6 padding, 16px icon wrap). Touch target is always 48×48px minimum. XS is defined in Figma for Primary/Secondary/Negative only (not Tertiary).

type.description: Semantic intent. Primary = brand blue. Secondary = neutral muted. Tertiary = lightest. Negative = destructive.

text.description: Visible label text. Also used as accessible name when showText is false.

leadingIcon.description: Material Symbols ligature name (e.g. 'add', 'check'). Rendered when showLeadingIcon is true.

trailingIcon.description: Material Symbols ligature name (e.g. 'arrow_forward'). Rendered when showTrailingIcon is true.

showText.description: When false: icon-only button. ariaLabel is required when showText is false.

loading.description: Replaces content with ButtonSpinner. Sets aria-busy='true'. Implicitly disables the button.

onClick.description: Click / keyboard activation handler. Not called when disabled or loading.

ariaLabel.description: Overrides accessible name. Required when showText is false (icon-only).

className.description: Additional CSS class on the outer <button> element.

accessibility.focusRing: 6px white halo + 2px brand ring via box-shadow on Container.Main

module-icon.description: The twelve Amplify module marks, in two treatments and three colour variants, on a 16x16 canvas.
module-icon.moduleNote: Size is DEPTH of colour, not of shape: Two Color resolves the module's base and subtle identity colours, One Color draws the whole mark in the base colour (Figma's own variant, not a tint), and Mono resolves every path to currentColor. The 23 --module-* identity properties are declared ON the component and resolve through PRIMITIVES rather than semantics, because a module's colour is its identity and must not flip with the theme: Giving is the same blue in Light and Midnight. This is the one place in the system where reading a primitive directly is correct. CHANGED 2026-10-01: the Figma canvas moved from 24x24 to 16x16 and the single Color value `Full` became `Two Color` plus `One Color`, so every path coordinate is re-exported rather than rescaled. `color="full"` survives as a deprecated alias for `two-color`. The default size follows the canvas and is now 16. BOTH TREATMENTS NOW HAVE ARTWORK. Figma's Style axis maps onto the prop `treatment`, not `style`, because `style` is already the CSS style object on every React component. Base is 38 paths across the twelve modules, Rippled is 66, and they are genuinely different geometry rather than a modifier. Rippled exists in Two Color and Mono only, so asking for rippled plus one-color returns Two Color rather than a flat treatment the design does not define. Equip's gradient coordinates differ by treatment, because the Rippled artwork reaches further across the frame; within a treatment all its gradients are byte-identical so one def serves them all. The three demos that carry the artwork inline (top-nav, nav-shell, module-icon) are GENERATED by scripts/sync-demo-module-icon.js, which is chained into build-dist: they used to be byte-identical 35kB hand-copies and all three silently kept drawing the 24 canvas after the module was updated.

icon.description: The one place Pathway renders an icon, plus the two wrappers Figma nests around it.

font.note: A Pathway icon is a FONT, not a file. There is no per-icon asset: one variable font carries every glyph and an icon is its NAME written as text. The name is the folder name in the source repo.

measured.actionIcon: Small 36x36 box / 24 state layer / 12 glyph; Base 44 / 28 / 14; Large 48 / 32 / 16. The fill belongs on the LAYER, which is smaller than the target.
measured.sizeRule: Size is the FRAME, never the drawn vector. Figma nests a 24 wrapper, a 16 frame and a ~12 vector; size={16} reproduces the 16.
measured.axes: FILL 0 or 1, READ FROM FIGMA per component. wght 400 and GRAD 0 everywhere. opsz matched to the font size.

icon.gaps: Modern's shadow has no exact token: Figma is 0 1 2 plus two inner shadows, and --elevation-widget (0 2 8 -2) is the nearest. The inner shadows are dropped as an Untitled UI flourish. The Positive glyph takes On Subtle rather than the exact-hex On Strong, because On Strong is for a solid fill and this sits on a Subtle one; 11.94:1 against 15.4:1, both AAA. The glyph components nested in Pathway components (add, search, expand_more, expand_less, moving) are REMOTE, so there is nothing per glyph to map; in code they are a name string.
icon.note: Created 2026-10-07 because every Figma icon component had NO code to point at: Code Connect listed them with no path and no link, and six components each carried a private Icon or Glyph helper that nothing could import. ActionIcon moved here out of widget.jsx, where it was private despite being nested 30 times in that very Figma set.
icon.figmaFixed: DisplayIcon was bound in the file on 2026-10-08. An earlier report claimed its Color axis had NO tokens, which was WRONG: the bindings live on the Container frame and on the _shape vector inside the glyph instance, not on the variant or the instance, so a reader checking those two nodes concludes it is unbound. The real defects, found by reading all 21 variants: only 4 of 21 glyphs were bound; two of those used HUE-NAMED tokens (Foreground/Static/Amethyst/Bold and /Green/Bold, neither of which is even in the local variable set any more); Neutral drew Fill/Action/Secondary/Hover, an ACTION token on a decorative element; Info drew Fill/Static/Brand/Faint, and Faint has no paired On Subtle foreground; and every Container carried a paint STYLE as well as a variable. All 42 bindings now use the meaning-named Subtle/On Subtle pairing, the styles are cleared, and each Color keeps the hue it already rendered: Accent is amethyst (Info) and Info is brand, which is the file's own history.
